title: tests(attachments): pin unscoped-multi-delete clause C3 end to end, and correct the ledger that still calls it broken
body:
Fixes #9483

QA run #9401 listed `attachments-storage.attach-requires-parent-edit` clause C3 —
*"an unscoped multi-delete (no id AND no where) is refused outright (#4757)"* — as
unpinned. #9724 correctly declined to pin it: measured end to end, the refusal did
not fire, and pinning the behaviour of the day would have turned the eventual fix
red. That product gap (#9719) was closed by PR #9797 and widened to the update verb
by #9974.

**So the first deliverable here was re-verification, not test-authoring.** Walking
the card's clause list against the merged ref:

| clause set | verdict on `main` | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `download-authz-both-sides` C3 | pinned already (#9724) | `attachments-public-read-acl.dogfood.test.ts`, ref accurate |
| `download-authz-both-sides` C4 | manual by design | browser denial copy; ref's scope note says so |
| `read-inherits-parent-rls` C1 + C3 | pinned already (#9724) | count-parity + scan-cap pins, refs accurate |
| `attach-requires-parent-edit` C3 | **behaviour pinned, ledger stale, dogfood blind** | this PR |

Nothing #9724 landed is re-pinned.

## The ledger was wrong in the dangerous direction

`automated.ref` and `knownGaps` still read **"⛔ CLAUSE 3 IS NOT PINNED … the #4757
'refused outright' rule does NOT fire through ObjectQL.delete"**. That has been false
since 2026-08-19. The next Tier-1 runner would have been told that a shipped, working
safety guard is broken.

## The measured detection gap — why a new pin was needed at all

"Refused outright" and "the per-row gate refused one of the rows" answer with the
**same code**, so they are indistinguishable on a fixture whose rows split
entitled/not — which is exactly the fixture the landed block uses.

Measured, not argued: with `dispatchUnscopedMultiWrite` removed from **both**
`sys_attachment` registrations, `service-storage` rebuilt and the ablation proven
live in `dist/` (`ablation-dist-preflight.mjs` → *"marker absent from all 6 built
files"*), the existing block stays **5/5 GREEN**. It cannot see the clause it is
named for.

The new block seeds the one fixture that separates them — a caller who uploaded
**every** matched row, whom the per-row gate would wave through — plus the
empty-table (zero-match) limb, which no handler-only fix could ever reach.

## Ablation (both legs rebuilt, both dist-preflighted)

Same mutation, against the extended suite: **3 failed | 7 passed**, exactly as
predicted, each red for its predicted reason — a matching count alone is not a pass.

| case | predicted | observed |
|---|---|---|
| block 1 · "refused OUTRIGHT" | red — wrong message | `expected Error: Cannot delete attachment … to match object` (the per-row gate answered) |
| block 2 · uploader of every row | red — resolves, the wipe | `promise resolved "2" instead of rejecting` — #9719's measurement reproduced |
| block 2 · empty table | red — resolves | `promise resolved "+0" instead of rejecting` |
| block 2 · scoped sweep (both sides) | green — no cascade | green |

Restore leg: *"marker present in 2 built files"*; tree clean, `src` count back to 2.

## Also corrected in the item

- **`oracle` `api` → `test`, and step 6 rewritten.** The step prescribed a REST probe
  the item's own `knownGaps` says the HTTP lane cannot express
  (`DeleteManyDataRequestSchema` requires an ids list, #3897). A runner following it
  would score a schema rejection as the refusal — green for the wrong reason.
- **`where: {}` re-documented.** It reaches the same verdict by a *different* rule;
  the whole-operation dispatch is deliberately scoped to a delete with no `where` at
  all. The case now asserts the **per-row** message, so that boundary goes red rather
  than silently agreeing if #4757's refusal ever widens.
- Source list: `MULTI_DELETE_AUTH_LIMIT` → `MULTI_WRITE_AUTH_LIMIT`.

## Verification — union at `e3da4cda` (the final commit)

`Test Files 1 passed (1)` / `Tests 10 passed (10)`.

Gates green, each read from its own verdict line: `check:platform-checklist` (15
areas, 205 items) · `check:nul-bytes` (6349 files) · `check:engine-double-contract` ·
`check:where-matcher` · `check:test-source-alias` · `check:cross-package-test-inputs` ·
`check:type-check-coverage` · `check:query-options-erasure` · `check:doc-authoring` ·
`check:doc-formula-expressions` · `check:published-files` · `check:slot-lookup` ·
`check:type-source-resolution` · `check-ci-filter-parity` · `check-plugin-teardown-shape` ·
`check-affected-docs` · spec `check:empty-state` / `check:liveness` /
`check:strictness-ledger` / `check:variant-docs` · `@objectstack/dogfood typecheck`.

`check:type-check-debt --re-measure` **refused first** on an unbuilt closure — recorded
as NOT MEASURED, then the closure was built exactly as `lint.yml` does and it re-ran
green: *"33 ledger entr(ies) re-measured in 233.9s, 1897 raw tsc error(s) total, none
above its recorded number."* No baseline moved.

ESLint narrowed to the diff and the narrowing is measured, not assumed: 2 files
submitted, `--format json` reports the `.ts` file linted with **0 errors / 0 warnings**
and the `.json` *"ignored because no matching configuration was supplied"* — so eslint's
own config puts it outside the linted population. Type-aware linting is not enabled
(`eslint.config.mjs` states no `parserOptions.project`, no typed rules), so this diff
cannot move the verdict on any untouched file.

No changeset: `@objectstack/dogfood` is `private: true` and the diff is tests plus
checklist prose, so this releases nothing — `skip-changeset` applied, per this repo's
route 2 (an empty-frontmatter changeset is explicitly the wrong route here).
